definition_zh: 逻辑；逻辑学；推理；条理；内在道理
definition_en: the study of valid reasoning; a system or process of reasoning; the sense or rationale behind something
core_image: 一排排前提像齿轮咬合，转动第一只，结论便被迫转到终点
scene: 辩论赛上，反方用三段论一步步推进。 Their logic took the other side's premise and pushed it until it contradicted itself, and the judges drew the chain on paper.
sceneCN: 这里 logic 是「逻辑推理」（第 2 个义项：从前提推出结论的过程）；句意：他们的推理拿对方的前提一步步往下推，直到自相矛盾，评委在纸上画出这条推理链。图中可辨识物件：辩论台、写满前提与箭头的纸、评委的笔、计时器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 逻辑；逻辑学；推理；条理；内在道理

collocations.zh: 顺着推理走；按逻辑推下去

forms.label: 复数（多于一个，指多套逻辑体系）

derivatives.zh: 不合逻辑的；缺乏条理的

senses.title: The discipline: the study of valid inference
senses.titleCN: 学科：研究有效推理的逻辑学
senses.definition: the branch of philosophy and science that studies the forms of valid reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 研究有效推理形式的哲学与科学分支
senses.example: She studied logic before turning to computer science.
senses.exampleCN: 她在转向计算机科学之前学过逻辑学。
senses.why: Greek logikē tekhnē was the 'art of reasoning', built on logos, 'word, reason, account'. The first sense is therefore the organized discipline that teaches how accounts must hang together.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 logikē tekhnē 是“推理之术”，建立在 logos“言词、理性、说明”之上。因此第一个义项就是教人如何让论述环环相扣的那门有组织的学科。

senses.title: The process: reasoning from premises
senses.definition: the process of drawing a conclusion from premises according to consistent rules
senses.definitionCN: 依照一致的规则从前提出发推出结论的过程
senses.example: The detective's logic led her to the only possible suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探的推理把她引向唯一可能的嫌疑人。
senses.why: The discipline becomes an activity: a mind moves from what it accepts to what follows. The gears of the core image turn, and the conclusion is carried along whether one likes it or not.
senses.whyCN: 学科变成一种活动：心智从它接受的前提走向必然得出的结论。核心意象里的齿轮转动，结论不管人喜不喜欢都被带到终点。

senses.title: Sensible consistency: there is logic in it
senses.titleCN: 条理：事情说得通、前后一致
senses.definition: the quality of being sensible, consistent, or reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 明智、前后一致或合乎情理的性质
senses.example: There is a certain logic in her decision, even if I dislike it.
senses.exampleCN: 她的决定自有其道理，尽管我并不喜欢。
senses.why: When an account holds together, we say it has logic. The word moves from the formal rules to the everyday impression that nothing in the story contradicts anything else.
senses.whyCN: 当一个说法前后立得住，我们就说它有逻辑。这个词从形式规则转向日常印象：故事里没有任何一处与另一处相矛盾。

senses.title: Inner rationale: the logic of a situation
senses.titleCN: 内在道理：局势自身的运行逻辑
senses.definition: the underlying rationale that makes a situation, system, or institution work as it does
senses.definitionCN: 使某种局势、制度或体系如此运作的深层道理
senses.example: The logic of the market rewards speed over craftsmanship.
senses.exampleCN: 市场的逻辑奖励速度，而不是手艺。
senses.why: A system has its own forced sequence: given its rules, certain outcomes follow. Calling this its logic treats the system as an argument whose conclusion is already built in.
senses.whyCN: 一个体系有自己的强制序列：给定其规则，某些结果就会随之而来。把它称为“逻辑”，就是把该体系当作一个结论早已内置的论证。

senses.title: A formal system: Aristotelian, modal, fuzzy logic
senses.titleCN: 形式体系：亚里士多德逻辑、模态逻辑、模糊逻辑
senses.definition: a particular formal system of rules for valid inference, such as classical, modal, or fuzzy logic
senses.definitionCN: 某一套关于有效推理的形式规则体系，如经典逻辑、模态逻辑或模糊逻辑
senses.example: Modal logic adds rules for statements about necessity and possibility.
senses.exampleCN: 模态逻辑为关于必然性与可能性的陈述增加了规则。
senses.why: There is not one logic but many. Each system fixes its own symbols, axioms, and permitted moves, so 'a logic' names a game with explicit rules rather than reasoning in general.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑不止一套，而是有许多套。每个体系固定自己的符号、公理与允许的步骤，因此“一套逻辑”命名的是一场规则明确的游戏，而不是一般意义上的推理。

senses.title: Digital logic: gates and circuits
senses.titleCN: 数字逻辑：逻辑门与电路
senses.definition: the branch of electronics in which signals are combined by Boolean operations such as AND, OR, and NOT
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中用电平信号按与、或、非等布尔运算组合的分支
senses.example: The chip contains thousands of logic gates.
senses.exampleCN: 这块芯片包含数千个逻辑门。
senses.why: Formal rules become hardware: true and false turn into high and low voltage, and a gate output follows its inputs exactly as a conclusion follows premises. The abstract chain is now etched in silicon.
senses.whyCN: 形式规则变成硬件：真与假转为高电平与低电平，逻辑门的输出严格跟随输入，就像结论跟随前提。抽象的推理链此时被刻进硅片。

senses.title: Program logic: rules that decide behaviour
senses.titleCN: 程序逻辑：决定行为的规则
senses.definition: in computing, the set of rules in a program that determine how it responds to input
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，程序中决定如何响应输入的一组规则
senses.example: The payment logic rejects cards with expired dates.
senses.exampleCN: 支付逻辑会拒绝过期日期的银行卡。
senses.why: Software encodes if-then structures: under condition A, do B. Business logic is the reasoning of an institution written as executable rules, so the same word covers both thought and machine.
senses.whyCN: 软件把“如果—那么”结构编码：在条件 A 下执行 B。业务逻辑就是把机构的推理写成可执行的规则，因此同一个词同时覆盖思维与机器。

senses.title: Argument structure: the chain from premise to conclusion
senses.titleCN: 论证结构：从前提到结论的链条
senses.definition: the structure of an argument, especially the relation between its premises and its conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 论证的结构，尤指前提与结论之间的关系
senses.example: The essay has a clear logic: each paragraph answers the objection raised before.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章逻辑清晰：每一段都回应前一段提出的反驳。
senses.why: Here logic is neither a discipline nor an inner rationale but the visible skeleton of a text. Each part must be held by the part before it, or the chain of proof breaks.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 logic 既不是学科，也不是内在道理，而是文本可见的骨架。每一部分都必须被前一部分扣住，否则证明链就断了。

senses.title: Usage boundary: countable only as a system
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：只有指“体系”时才可数
senses.definition: a usage limit: logic is usually uncountable; a logic or logics is used only for distinct formal systems, and logic is not a synonym for opinion or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 用法限制：logic 通常不可数；a logic 或 logics 只用于不同的形式体系，且 logic 不是 opinion 或 feeling 的同义词
senses.example: His anger is real, but it is not an argument in logic.
senses.exampleCN: 他的愤怒是真实的，但它在逻辑上不构成论据。
senses.why: The mass noun names reasoning as a substance, not a set of opinions. Counting begins only when separate rule-systems are compared. Emotion can motivate a claim, but it cannot supply the force of a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个不可数名词把推理视作一种“质料”，而不是一堆观点。只有比较彼此独立的规则体系时才开始计数。情绪可以促使人提出主张，却不能提供结论的力量。

intro.en: Logic reaches English through Greek, Latin, and French. The chain logos to logikē to logica to logique is well documented; the Indo-European root *leg- is generally believed rather than certain.
intro.cn: logic 经由希腊语、拉丁语和法语进入英语。从 logos 到 logikē、logica、logique 的链条有清楚记载；其印欧词根 *leg- 只是一般认为，并非确定。

items.en: Greek logos meant 'word, speech, account, reason'. It could name a story told, an explanation given, or the rational order behind things.
items.cn: 希腊语 logos 意为“言词、言语、说明、理性”。它既可以指讲述的故事、给出的解释，也可以指事物背后的理性秩序。

items.en: Logos is generally traced to PIE *leg- 'to gather, pick up', specifically 'to pick words'. Speaking is pictured as gathering words and putting them in order; the deeper link is generally believed, not proved.
items.cn: logos 一般追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“采集、拾起”，尤指“挑选词语”。说话被想象成把词语采集起来并排成次序；这一更深联系属于一般认为是，而非已经证明。

items.en: Logikē (tekhnē) meant the 'art of reasoning', the skill of using logoi well. Aristotle's works on argument turned that skill into a systematic study.
items.cn: logikē (tekhnē) 意为“推理之术”，即善用 logoi 的技能。亚里士多德关于论证的著作把这种技能变成了系统研究。

items.en: Latin logica and Old French logique carried the word westward. In the medieval curriculum logic was one of the three basic arts, alongside grammar and rhetoric.
items.cn: 拉丁语 logica 与古法语 logique 把这个词带到西方。在中世纪课程中，逻辑学与语法、修辞并列为三门基础技艺。

items.en: English logic appears in the 14c. Mathematical logic develops in the 19c., and digital logic in the 20c. gives the old art of reasoning a silicon body.
items.cn: 英语 logic 出现于 14 世纪。数理逻辑在 19 世纪发展起来，数字逻辑在 20 世纪给这门古老的推理之术装上了硅制的身体。

note.en: The first group shares the logos root or the log- shape; the second separates the discipline from reasoning, rationale, consistency, and one specific inference type.
note.cn: 第一组共享 logos 词根或 log- 词形；第二组把“逻辑学”与推理、根据、一致性以及一种具体推理类型分开。

entries.definition: following the rules of logic; sensible and consistent. It is the adjective built on logic.
entries.definitionCN: 符合逻辑规则的；有条理的。它是 logic 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: the organized movement and supply of goods and people. It comes from Greek logistikos 'skilled in calculating', also from logos.
entries.definitionCN: 货物与人员的有组织调运和供给。它来自希腊语 logistikos“擅长计算”，同样出自 logos。

entries.definition: a symbol or design used as a brand mark. It is shortened from logotype, from Greek logos 'word'.
entries.definitionCN: 用作品牌标记的符号或图案。它由 logotype 缩略而来，源自希腊语 logos“言词”。

entries.definition: the mental process of thinking things through. It is broader than logic and can include informal, practical thought.
entries.definitionCN: 把事情想通的思维过程。它比 logic 宽泛，可以包括非正式的、实践性的思考。

entries.definition: the reasons or explanation behind a decision or system. It names the content, not the formal study of inference.
entries.definitionCN: 某一决定或体系背后的理由或解释。它命名内容，而不是对推理的形式研究。

entries.definition: the property of parts fitting together without contradiction. It is one test of logic, not logic itself.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分彼此相容、不矛盾的性质。它是逻辑的一项检验，而不是逻辑本身。

entries.definition: inference from general premises to a necessary conclusion. It is one branch of logic, not the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 从一般前提到必然结论的推理。它是逻辑学的一个分支，而不是整个领域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: logos as word and reason, the real phrases formal logic and logic gate, and the everyday 'there is no logic in it'.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：作为言词与理性的 logos、真实短语 formal logic 与 logic gate，以及日常说法“毫无逻辑”。

normal.en: Logos meant 'word, account, reason'; logic is the art of making an account hold together.
normal.cn: logos 意为“言词、说明、理性”；logic 就是让一套说明站得住的技术。

normal.en: Formal logic writes the rules down: if the premises are true and the form is valid, the conclusion must be true.
normal.cn: formal logic 把规则写下来：如果前提为真且形式有效，结论必然为真。

normal.en: The logic of a situation is its inner forced sequence: given those rules, this outcome follows.
normal.cn: the logic of a situation 指局势内在的强制序列：给定那些规则，这个结果就会随之而来。

normal.en: A logic gate is the same reasoning in hardware: high and low inputs produce an output by rule.
normal.cn: 逻辑门是同一套推理的硬件版本：高、低输入按规则产生输出。

normal.en: Logical and illogical split the world into what follows and what contradicts itself.
normal.cn: logical 与 illogical 把世界分成两类：推得下去的，和自相矛盾的。

abstract.en: A chain of premises: each link is forced, and the last link cannot refuse the pull of the first.
abstract.cn: 一条前提链：每一环都是被迫的，最后一环无法拒绝第一环的拉力。

abstract.en: A transparent machine: put premises in at the top, and only the conclusion comes out at the bottom; emotion stays outside.
abstract.cn: 一台透明的机器：前提从上方放入，只有结论从下方出来；情绪留在机器之外。

abstract.en: A skeleton that holds an argument upright: remove one bone and the whole body of proof collapses.
abstract.cn: 一副撑起论证的骨架：抽掉一根骨头，整个证明的身体就塌了。

examples.en: The argument is elegant, but its logic is flawed at the second step.
examples.cn: 这个论证很漂亮，但它的逻辑在第二步就有漏洞。

examples.en: There is a simple logic to her method: test the cheapest fix first.
examples.cn: 她的方法有一个简单的内在道理：先试最便宜的修法。

examples.en: Modern processors are built from millions of logic gates.
examples.cn: 现代处理器由数百万个逻辑门构成。

dict_mnemonic.text: “老季克”——老季讲话条理清楚，句句都推得下去 → logic 逻辑

root: 希腊语 logos“言词、理性、说明”，经 logikē tekhnē“推理之术”而来；核心是“用有章法的言词把道理讲通”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of logic, all from logos as ordered speech: the discipline, the act of reasoning, the feel of consistency, the rationale inside a system, a formal rule-system, silicon gates, program rules, the skeleton of an argument, and the boundary of countable uses.
sensesIntro.cn: logic 的九个义项都出自 logos 作为“有秩序的言词”：学科、推理行为、前后一致的感觉、体系内的道理、形式规则体系、硅片上的门、程序规则、论证骨架，以及可数用法的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ordered words lock together and force a conclusion.
core.cn: 核心意象：有次序的言词彼此咬合，迫使结论出现。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS SYSTEMS: logic is both the study of valid form and the named formal systems it compares.
branches.cn: 学科及其体系：logic 既是对有效形式的研究，也是它所比较的各套具名形式体系。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SKELETON: reasoning moves from premise to conclusion, and the written argument shows that chain.
branches.cn: 行为与骨架：推理从前提到结论，书面论证则展示这条链。

branches.en: CONSISTENCY AND RATIONALE: an account holds together, and a system carries its own forced logic.
branches.cn: 一致性与内在道理：一套说明前后立得住，一个体系则带有自身强制的逻辑。

branches.en: MACHINES: Boolean gates and program rules turn inference into hardware and code.
branches.cn: 机器：布尔门与程序规则把推理变成硬件与代码。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: logic is mass-noun reasoning, countable only when separate systems are meant.
branches.cn: 边界：logic 是不可数的推理，只有指彼此独立的体系时才可数。

intro.en: Logic is a Greek-derived noun ending in -ic. English builds the adjective with -al, the adverb with -ally, the person with -ian, and the negative with il-.
intro.cn: logic 是源自希腊语、以 -ic 结尾的名词。英语用 -al 构成形容词，用 -ally 构成副词，用 -ian 构成人物名词，用 il- 构成否定。

latinIntro.en: The family rests on Greek logos 'word, reason'. Dialogue, monologue, logistics and analogy all contain that same second element or its derivative.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族建立在希腊语 logos“言词、理性”上。dialogue、monologue、logistics、analogy 都含有同一词素或其派生形式。

items.meaning: following the rules of logic; sensible
items.meaningCN: 逻辑的；合乎逻辑的（-al 表示“与……有关”）
items.example: That is the logical conclusion from the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 那是从证据得出的合乎逻辑的结论。

items.meaning: in a way that follows from the premises
items.meaningCN: 逻辑上；合乎逻辑地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Logically, the second claim depends on the first.
items.exampleCN: 从逻辑上说，第二个主张依赖于第一个。

items.meaning: a person who studies or works with logic
items.meaningCN: 逻辑学家（-ian 表示从事该学科的人）
items.example: The logician rewrote the proof in symbols.
items.exampleCN: 这位逻辑学家用符号重写了证明。

items.meaning: not following from the premises; inconsistent
items.meaningCN: 不合逻辑的；缺乏条理的（il- 表示否定）
items.example: It is illogical to expect a different result from the same input.
items.exampleCN: 指望同样的输入产生不同的结果是不合逻辑的。

items.example: The noun is the source of logic and of -logy.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 logic 与 -logy 的来源。

items.example: The stem appears in dialogue, catalogue and logic.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 dialogue、catalogue 与 logic。

items.example: It shapes logical, the adjective built on logic.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 logical 这一形容词。

items.example: The ending marks logic as a discipline, logike in Greek.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 logic 标为一门学问，希腊语作 logike。

items.meaning: a formal argument from two premises
items.example: The syllogism is the oldest tool of formal logic.
items.exampleCN: 三段论是形式逻辑最古老的工具。

latinEntries.meaning: a conversation between two or more people
latinEntries.meaningCN: 对话；对白（dia- 表示“之间”，logos 表示“言词”）

latinEntries.meaning: a long speech by one person
latinEntries.meaningCN: 独白；长篇独语（mono- 表示“单一”）

latinEntries.meaning: the organized supply and movement of goods and people
latinEntries.meaningCN: 物流；后勤（源自“擅长计算”，与 logos 同族）

latinEntries.meaning: a comparison based on a shared relation
latinEntries.meaningCN: 类比；类推（按相同的比例或关系作比较）

definition_zh: 螺栓；门闩；猛冲；一道闪电
definition_en: a metal bar that slides across to lock a door
core_image: 夜里插紧的门闩
scene: 睡前她把门闩插好。 She bolted the door before going to bed.
sceneCN: 这里 bolt 是「门闩；插上闩」（第 2 个义项：门上滑动的锁）；句意是睡前她把门闩好。

senses.title: A metal fastener
senses.definition: a thick metal pin used to hold parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把部件固定在一起的粗金属销
senses.example: The mechanic tightened every bolt on the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工把车轮上的每颗螺栓都拧紧了。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming the metal pin that shoots through a hole.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指穿过孔洞的金属销。

senses.title: A bar that locks a door
senses.definition: a sliding bar that keeps a door closed
senses.definitionCN: 让门保持关闭的滑动横杆
senses.example: She bolted the door before going to bed.
senses.exampleCN: 睡前她把门闩好。
senses.why: A door bar works like a bolt shot into place.
senses.whyCN: 门上的横杆就像射入锁孔的螺栓。

senses.title: To run away suddenly
senses.definition: to move or run away very suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然快速移动或逃走
senses.example: The horse bolted when it heard the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 马听到响声就惊跑了。
senses.why: Something that bolts leaves like a bolt shot from a gun.
senses.whyCN: bolt 的离开就像子弹被射出一样。

senses.title: A flash of lightning
senses.definition: a sudden flash of lightning
senses.definitionCN: 突然划过的闪电
senses.example: A bolt of lightning lit the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 一道闪电照亮了天空。
senses.why: Lightning looks like a metal shaft thrown across the sky.
senses.whyCN: 闪电看起来像一支金属箭划过天空。

intro.en: Bolt is an Old English word for an arrow, and the arrow idea runs through its senses.
intro.cn: bolt 是古英语中表示箭的词，箭的意象贯穿它的各个义项。

items.en: bolt meant a short thick arrow.
items.cn: bolt 指短而粗的箭。

items.en: bolt named the metal pin of a crossbow.
items.cn: bolt 指弩上的金属箭。

items.en: bolt became a metal pin that fastens parts.
items.cn: bolt 变成固定部件的金属销。

items.en: the door bolt and the flash of lightning were both named.
items.cn: 门闩与闪电都用这个词命名。

items.en: bolt covers fastening, locking, running and lightning.

definition_zh: 毒药；毒物；下毒；污染；毒害
definition_en: a substance that harms or kills when it enters the body; also to put such a substance into something, to pollute a natural resource, or to corrupt a mind or a relationship
core_image: 一只没有标签的深色小瓶放在高高的架子上，瓶口沾着干涸的痕迹，旁边的人伸手前先停了一下
scene: 厨房角落的柜子上放着一只没有标签的旧瓶子，孩子踮脚要去够，母亲一把把他拉开。 The faded label warned that the bottle contained a deadly poison.
sceneCN: 这里 poison 指「毒药、毒物」（第 1 个义项：进入身体后致病或致死的东西）；句意为褪色的标签警告说，这瓶里装着致命的毒药。图中可辨识物件：旧瓶子、模糊的标签、踮脚的孩子。

senses.title: A substance that harms or kills
senses.definition: a substance that causes illness or death when swallowed, breathed in or absorbed through the skin
senses.definitionCN: 吞下、吸入或经皮肤吸收后引起疾病或死亡的物质
senses.example: Rat poison must be kept away from children and pets.
senses.exampleCN: 灭鼠毒药必须放在儿童和宠物够不到的地方。
senses.why: Latin potio meant simply a drink, and because a prepared draught could heal or kill, the word slid towards the deadly kind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 potio 本只指「一饮」，而调好的药水既能治病也能致命，词义便滑向致命的那一类。

senses.title: To put poison into something
senses.definition: to add poison to food, drink or another substance, or to kill a person or animal that way
senses.definitionCN: 把毒物放进食物、饮料或其他物质里，或用这种方式杀死人或动物
senses.example: Someone had poisoned the well during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 有人夜里在水井里下了毒。
senses.why: Once the noun named the substance, plain conversion let English say what a person does with it, with no suffix added at all.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指认了这种物质，英语不必加任何后缀，直接转作动词就能说人拿它去做什么。

senses.title: To pollute a natural resource
senses.definition: to make water, air, soil or food harmful by adding a dangerous substance
senses.definitionCN: 通过加入危险物质使水、空气、土壤或食物变得有害
senses.example: Waste from the factory had poisoned the river for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂排出的废料把这条河污染了好几英里。
senses.why: Poison need not be administered on purpose; anything that makes a shared resource unsafe behaves like poison, so the verb widens to pollution.
senses.whyCN: 毒物不必被人有意投入；任何让公共资源变得不安全的东西都起着毒物的作用，于是动词扩展到污染。

senses.title: To corrupt a mind or a relationship
senses.definition: to spoil someone's mind, trust or a relationship so that it stops working well
senses.definitionCN: 败坏某人的心智、信任或一段关系，使其不再正常运转
senses.example: Years of rumour had poisoned the friendship between the two families.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的流言败坏了这两家人之间的友谊。
senses.why: The body is not the only thing that can be poisoned: a mind fed on lies or a bond fed on suspicion shows the same damage, so the word moves into feeling.
senses.whyCN: 能被毒害的不只是身体：被谎言喂养的心智、被猜疑喂养的关系会显出同样的损伤，于是这个词进入情感领域。

intro.en: Poison began as a Latin word for a drink, narrowed into the deadly draught, and then widened again to pollution and to corrupted minds.
intro.cn: poison 最初是拉丁语中表示「饮料」的词，先收窄为致命的一剂，后来又扩展到污染与败坏的心智。

items.en: The verb potare meant to drink, and it named the ordinary act of taking liquid.
items.cn: 动词 potare 意为喝，指的是喝下液体的平常动作。

items.en: The noun potio was a drink or a draught, including a prepared potion that might cure or harm.
items.cn: 名词 potio 指饮料或一剂，也包括调好的、可能治病也可能伤人的药水。

items.en: Old French reshaped potio into poison, keeping the sense of a prepared drink and adding the sense of a deadly one.
items.cn: 古法语把 potio 改造成 poison，既保留「调制好的饮品」义，又添上「致命的一剂」义。

items.en: Middle English used poison for any harmful substance and, by conversion, for the act of administering it.
items.cn: 中古英语用 poison 指任何有害物质，并通过词性转换指投入这种物质的行为。

items.en: Modern English widened it to polluted rivers and poisoned minds, and kept compounds such as poison gas and food poisoning.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到被污染的河流与被毒害的心智，并保留 poison gas、food poisoning 这类复合说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the poison family and one close cousin from the same drink word; the near-meaning group gathers animal and chemical terms for harmful substances.
note.cn: 形近组收 poison 词族，以及同出「饮料」一词的近亲；近义组收指有害物质的动物性与化学性词语。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with something you swallow, and every later sense keeps that image of a substance entering where it should not.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一件被吞下的东西开始，此后每个义项都保留着「有东西进入本不该进入之处」的画面。

normal.en: Potare means to drink and potio is a draught, so poison began as something you swallow rather than something that burns.
normal.cn: potare 意为喝，potio 是一剂饮品，所以 poison 最初是被吞下的东西，而不是灼人的东西。

normal.en: French reshaped potio into poison while keeping the sense of a prepared drink, which is why the word still sounds medicinal.
normal.cn: 法语把 potio 改成 poison，同时保留「调制好的一剂」的意思，所以这个词至今带着药水味。

normal.en: Poison is noun and verb in one shape, a plain English conversion with no ending added.
normal.cn: poison 名词与动词同形，是英语里不加词尾的朴素转换。

normal.en: Poisonous adds -ous, full of, and works as the adjective; poisoning adds -ing and names the act or the resulting illness.
normal.cn: poisonous 加 -ous，意为「充满……的」，作形容词；poisoning 加 -ing，指下毒行为或由此引起的中毒。

normal.en: Modern English keeps compounds such as poison gas and food poisoning, where the old noun does the work of an adjective.
normal.cn: 现代英语保留 poison gas 与 food poisoning 这类复合词，旧的名称在里面起着形容词的作用。

abstract.en: A word for a drink becoming a word for death is a reminder that the same prepared cup can go either way.
abstract.cn: 一个表示饮料的词变成表示死亡的词，提醒人：同样一只调好的杯子可以走向两个方向。

abstract.en: The move from a bottle to a river to a friendship shows English trusting one image to cover very different kinds of harm.
abstract.cn: 从瓶子到河流再到友情，可见英语放心地用同一幅画面覆盖差别极大的伤害。

abstract.en: To speak of poisoned trust is to treat a feeling as a body with its own circulation, which can be tainted from inside.
abstract.cn: 说信任被毒害，就是把一种感受当成有自身循环的身体，可以从内部被污染。

examples.en: The berries look harmless but contain a strong poison.
examples.cn: 这些浆果看着无害，却含有强烈的毒素。

examples.en: Industrial waste has poisoned the groundwater.

examples.en: Resentment had slowly poisoned their partnership.

intro.en: Curriculum is Latin for a running or a racecourse, from currere, to run; a course of study is a track learners run along.
intro.cn: curriculum 在拉丁语里意为「跑」或「跑道」，出自 currere（跑）；一门课程就是学生要跑的那条道。

items.en: Currere meant to run, and curriculum meant a running.
items.cn: currere 意为跑，curriculum 意为奔跑。

items.en: Curriculum also named the track a chariot ran on.
items.cn: curriculum 也指战车奔跑的跑道。

items.en: Roman writers used it for a fixed course of duties.
items.cn: 罗马作家用它指一套固定的职责流程。

items.en: Universities borrowed it for the course students run through.
items.cn: 大学借用它，指学生要跑完的课程。

items.en: Curriculum came to mean every subject a school teaches.
items.cn: curriculum 后来指一所学校教的全部科目。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the curr- stem, and the meaning group names other plans of study.
note.cn: 形近组共享 curr- 词干，近义组列出其他表示学习安排的说法。

由 marvelous 加表示性质的名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「奇妙；令人惊叹的性质」

senses.title: Extremely good and enjoyable
senses.definition: very good, pleasant or impressive, used in ordinary speech about things people enjoy
senses.definitionCN: 非常好、令人愉快或令人印象深刻，日常口语中用来夸人喜欢的事物
senses.example: We had a marvelous evening on the rooftop.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在屋顶上度过了一个极好的夜晚。
senses.why: Mirabilia named wonderful things, and everyday speech wore the sense down from causing wonder to plain very good, exactly as great and terrific slid from awe into approval.
senses.whyCN: mirabilia 原本指令人惊叹的事物，日常口语把这层意思从「引起惊叹」磨成了简单的「很好」，就像 great 与 terrific 也都从敬畏滑向了赞许。

senses.title: So beautiful or strange that the mind stops
senses.definition: so beautiful, strange or unlikely that it makes you stop and wonder at it
senses.definitionCN: 美、奇或不合常理到让人停下来发怔
senses.example: A marvelous green light spread over the ridge and would not fade.
senses.exampleCN: 一道奇妙的绿光铺过山脊，久久不散。
senses.why: Before it was praise, the word pointed at whatever mirari means to wonder at; that older sense survives whenever the thing itself, and not the pleasure, is what astonishes.
senses.whyCN: 在变成一句称赞之前，这个词指向 mirari（惊奇地看）所面对的东西；当令人吃惊的是事物本身而不是愉快感受时，这层较旧的意思就还活着。

senses.title: Brought about beyond the course of nature, an older use
senses.titleCN: 奇迹般的；超自然的（旧用法）
senses.definition: of an event, produced by a power outside the ordinary course of nature, a sense common in older religious writing
senses.definitionCN: 指某件事由自然常规之外的力量造成，这一义项多见于较早的宗教文字
senses.example: The old chronicle calls the healing marvelous rather than medical.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史记述这次痊愈为奇迹，而非医术。
senses.why: Mirabilis could describe what only a miracle explains, so the adjective kept a doorway to the supernatural long after it had learned to mean merely excellent.
senses.whyCN: mirabilis 可以形容只有神迹才解释得通的事，所以这个形容词在学会表示「很好」之后，仍长期保留着一扇通向超自然的门。

intro.en: Marvelous goes back to a Latin verb for wondering, through a noun for wonderful things, and it reached English by way of Old French with a noun and an adjective travelling together.
intro.cn: marvelous 可以追到拉丁语里表示「惊奇地看」的动词，中间经过一个指「奇妙之事」的名词，再随名词与形容词一同经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant to wonder at something, and its forms gave the whole family the idea of being looked at with astonishment.
items.cn: mirari 意为对某物感到惊奇，它的各种形式把「被惊讶地注视」这一观念给了整族词。

items.en: Mirabilis, wonderful or astonishing, described anything that provoked that look, from a strange animal to an unexpected healing.
items.cn: mirabilis 意为奇妙的、惊人的，用来描述任何引起那种注视的东西，从一只怪异的动物到一次意外的痊愈。

items.en: The neuter plural mirabilia meant wonderful things, and in that plural form it named the wonders collected in writing and in talk.
items.cn: 中性复数 mirabilia 意为「奇妙之事」，正是这个复数形式用来指被写进书里、说在口中的种种奇观。

items.en: Old French turned mirabilia into merveille, a wonder or marvel, and built the adjective merveillos on the same stem.
items.cn: 古法语把 mirabilia 变成 merveille，意为奇迹、奇观，并在同一词干上造出形容词 merveillos。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective as marvellous, the British spelling, and American usage later wrote marvelous; the noun marvel came from the same French word.
items.cn: 英语把形容词借作 marvellous，即英式拼写，美式用法后来写作 marvelous；名词 marvel 也出自同一个法语词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and the two spellings built on the Latin stem for wonder; the near group gathers other adjectives of praise and amazement.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「惊奇」词干上的名词与两种拼写；近义组收其他表示称赞与惊异的形容词。

entries.definition: A wonderful or astonishing thing, or to feel wonder at it.
entries.definitionCN: 令人惊叹的事物；也指对之感到惊奇；与 marvelous 出自同一个古法语词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of marvelous, with exactly the same senses.
entries.definitionCN: marvelous 的英式拼写，义项完全相同。

entries.definition: To regard someone or something with respect and warm approval, from Latin admirari built on mirari.
entries.definitionCN: 带着敬意与赞赏看待某人某物；出自拉丁语 admirari，其词基正是 mirari。

entries.definition: An extraordinary event that natural laws cannot explain, from Latin miraculum.
entries.definitionCN: 无法用自然规律解释的非凡事件；出自拉丁语 miraculum，与 marvelous 同源。

entries.definition: Extremely good, or filling you with wonder.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；或使人充满惊叹的。

entries.definition: Extremely good, or so strange that it seems imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；或奇到仿佛想象出来的。

entries.definition: So surprising that it is hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 令人吃惊到难以相信的。

entries.definition: Of the very highest quality.

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of a Latin verb for staring in astonishment, and its family keeps returning to wonder, the thing that causes it, and praise worn smooth by daily use.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语表示「惊奇地看」的动词长出来，它的同族词反复回到惊奇、引起惊奇的事物，以及被日常使用磨滑的称赞。

normal.en: Wonder is the seed: Latin mirari means to stare in astonishment, and mirabilis names whatever makes you stare.
normal.cn: 惊奇是种子：拉丁语 mirari 意为惊奇地看，mirabilis 则命名任何让你看住不动的东西。

normal.en: Mirabilia, wonderful things, passed into Old French merveille and gave English both marvel and the adjective marvellous.
normal.cn: mirabilia 意为奇妙之事，传进古法语成为 merveille，并给英语留下 marvel 与形容词 marvellous。

normal.en: The British spelling keeps the double l of the French ending, while American usage writes marvelous with a single l.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留法语词尾的双写 l，美式用法则把 marvelous 写成单写 l。

normal.en: Admire and miracle sit on the same Latin root, one naming the look you give, the other naming the event that earns it.
normal.cn: admire 与 miracle 站在同一个拉丁词根上，一个命名你给出的目光，一个命名赢得这目光的事件。

normal.en: The everyday sense of very good came later, when speakers spent a word of wonder as ordinary praise, as they did with terrific and fabulous.
normal.cn: 口语里「很好」的意思来得较晚，说话人把一个表示惊奇的字当普通称赞花出去，就像 terrific 与 fabulous 那样。

abstract.en: A child under a suddenly lit sky: the word begins in the open mouth, not in the judgement.
abstract.cn: 一个站在骤然亮起的天空下的孩子：这个词起于张开的口，不起于评判。

abstract.en: Praise is a fossil of awe; every cheap marvelous was once a genuine astonishment.
abstract.cn: 称赞是敬畏的化石；每一句廉价的 marvelous 都曾经是一次真心的惊奇。

abstract.en: Two l's or one, the same Latin wonder is still shut inside the word.
abstract.cn: 双写 l 也好，单写 l 也好，同一个拉丁语的惊奇仍被关在词里。

examples.en: We had a marvelous evening on the rooftop.
examples.cn: 我们在屋顶上度过了一个极好的夜晚。

examples.en: A marvelous green light spread over the ridge and would not fade.
examples.cn: 一道奇妙的绿光铺过山脊，久久不散。

examples.en: The old chronicle calls the healing marvelous rather than medical.
examples.cn: 那部旧编年史记述这次痊愈为奇迹，而非医术。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马佛勒斯」——马看见佛光铺满天空，惊讶得说不出话；记住 marvelous 是奇妙的、极好的。

root: 拉丁语 mirari（惊奇地看）→ mirabilis（奇妙的）→ 中性复数 mirabilia（奇妙之事）→ 古法语 merveille（奇迹）与 merveillos（奇妙的）→ 英语 marvel 与 marvelous；美式拼写省去一个 l。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the look of astonishment; the senses then divide into worn-down praise, the thing that truly amazes, and the older claim that something lies beyond nature.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是那副惊讶的目光；义项由此分成被磨平的称赞、真正令人惊异的事物，以及较早的「超出自然」之说。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child looking up at a sky suddenly filled with green light, mouth open, saying nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个孩子抬头看见天空忽然铺满绿光，张着嘴说不出话。

branches.en: a rooftop evening praised long after it ends
branches.cn: 屋顶的夜晚，结束后仍被反复称赞

branches.en: green light climbing over a dark ridge
branches.cn: 绿光爬上黑暗的山脊

branches.en: a chronicle calling a healing a wonder
branches.cn: 编年史把一次痊愈记作奇迹

branches.en: a crowd kneeling before a cure no doctor explains
branches.cn: 众人跪在医生解释不了的痊愈前

branches.en: a traveller telling the same story twice
branches.cn: 旅人把同一个故事讲了两遍

intro.en: A Latin verb for wondering, its adjective, the plural noun for wonders, two French forms and one English suffix hold the word together.
intro.cn: 一个表示惊奇的拉丁动词、它的形容词、指奇妙之事的名词复数、两个法语形式与一个英语后缀，把这个词撑在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin mirari, mirabilis and mirabilia are recorded and reliable; Old French merveille and merveillos are the accepted bridge to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mirari、mirabilis 与 mirabilia 有记录且可靠；古法语 merveille 与 merveillos 是被认可的进入英语的桥梁。

items.meaning: to wonder at, to be astonished
full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 不公平地；不公正地；不正当地
definition_en: in a way that gives people unequal or unjust treatment
core_image: 分苹果时，最大的那个总被递给同一个人
scene: 分奖金那天，干活最多的人拿得最少，大家低头不语。 He was treated unfairly.
sceneCN: 这里 unfairly 是「不公正地」（第 1 个义项：对待不公）；句意为他受到了不公正的对待。最大的果子总递给同一个人，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 副词去掉 -ly 的形容词形式，义为「不公平的」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不公平」
肯定形式加 -ly 的副词，义为「公平地；相当」
近义词，由 unjust 加 -ly 构成，义为「不公正地」

senses.title: In a way that gives unequal shares
senses.definition: in a way that gives some people less than they deserve
senses.definitionCN: 以让某些人所得少于应得的方式
senses.example: The prize money was unfairly divided among the players.
senses.exampleCN: 奖金在队员之间分得不公平。
senses.why: The adverb adds a manner to fair, and the negative prefix turns that manner into an unequal one.
senses.whyCN: 副词把「方式」加到 fair 上，否定前缀又把这种方变成了不平等的方式。

senses.title: By wronging a person
senses.definition: used with verbs such as blame, accuse, or punish to say the target was wronged
senses.definitionCN: 与 blame、accuse、punish 等动词连用，说明被对待者受了冤屈
senses.example: She was unfairly blamed for a mistake made by the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 整队犯的错却被不公正地算在她头上。
senses.why: Balance is broken by pushing the weight onto one person, which is exactly what the adverb describes.
senses.whyCN: 把重量全压到一个人身上就是失衡，这正是这个副词所描写的。

senses.title: Against the rules of a contest
senses.definition: in a manner that breaks agreed rules or takes a hidden advantage
senses.definitionCN: 以违背约定规则或暗中占便宜的方式
senses.example: One firm competed unfairly by copying a rival design.
senses.exampleCN: 一家公司抄袭对手的设计进行不正当竞争。
senses.why: Fair play is a game played by rule, so playing off-rule is doing it unfairly.
senses.whyCN: fair play 是按规则进行的比赛，不照规则出牌就是不公正。

senses.title: In employment or law
senses.definition: used in legal and workplace statements about treatment that cannot be justified
senses.definitionCN: 用于法律与职场陈述，指无法说明理由的对待
senses.example: The tribunal ruled that he had been dismissed unfairly.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭裁定他遭到了不公正的解雇。
senses.why: Legal language takes the everyday sense of a tilt and makes it a ground for a claim.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言把日常语中天平倾斜的感觉，变成了提出诉讼的理由。

senses.title: In a degree that seems excessive
senses.definition: used before a criticism to suggest the judgement goes too far
senses.definitionCN: 放在批评之前，暗示这个评判过头了
senses.example: It would be unfairly harsh to reject every draft.
senses.exampleCN: 把每一稿都否掉未免过分严厉。
senses.why: What is too harsh is not balanced, and the adverb carries that feeling of excess.
senses.whyCN: 过严即失衡，这个副词把那种过头的感觉带了出来。

intro.en: The adverb is built in English from fair, the negative prefix un-, and the ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个副词是英语自己拼起来的：fair 加否定前缀 un- 和词尾 -ly。

items.en: Fæger described something beautiful or pleasing.
items.cn: fæger 形容美丽、悦目之物。

items.en: Fair came to mean just and even-handed in judgement.
items.cn: fair 转为表示「公正、判断不偏」。

items.en: Un- was added in Middle English law, giving unfair for unjust dealings.
items.cn: 中古英语法律文中已加 un-，形成 unfair 指不公正的做法。

items.en: -ly turned the adjective into an adverb of manner in ordinary use.
items.cn: 在普通用法中，-ly 把形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: Unfairly now clusters with blame, accuse, and dismiss in legal and news texts.
items.cn: 如今在法律与新闻文本中，这个词常与 blame、accuse、dismiss 搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fair family, and the near-meaning group covers adverbs of injustice.
note.cn: 形近组收集 fair 词族，近义组覆盖表示不公的副词。

entries.definition: not equal or just
the quality of being unjust
equally, or to a moderate degree
always, without failing
entries.definitionCN: 总是；可靠地（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: in a way that is not morally right
incorrectly or unjustly
not in equal shares
in an equal and just way

normalIntro.en: The adverb is the adjective plus a manner ending, nothing more.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词就是形容词加一个方式词尾，再无别的。

normal.en: Unfairly is unfair plus -ly, the regular English adverb pattern.
normal.cn: unfairly 就是 unfair 加 -ly，英语规则的副词构词方式。

normal.en: Treated unfairly is the passive frame learners hear most.
normal.cn: treated unfairly 是学习者最常听到的被动搭配。

normal.en: Unfairly dismissed is a fixed phrase in employment law.
normal.cn: unfairly dismissed 是雇佣法中的固定说法。

normal.en: Unfairly blamed and unfairly accused both suggest a victim.
normal.cn: unfairly blamed 与 unfairly accused 都暗示有人受了冤。

normal.en: Fairly is the opposite in manner; fair is the opposite in quality.
normal.cn: 副词的反义是 fairly，形容词的反义是 fair。

abstract.en: Picture one child always getting the sliced-off, smaller half.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子每次都拿到切下去的、小的那一半。

abstract.en: See a referee turn his head at the foul.
abstract.cn: 看裁判在犯规那一刻把头转开。

abstract.en: Hear a verdict read out that the crowd meets with silence.
abstract.cn: 听宣判念出，人群以沉默回应。

examples.en: The two workers were unfairly paid for the same job.
examples.cn: 两个工人做同样的活，报酬却不公平。

examples.en: He felt he had been unfairly accused.
examples.cn: 他觉得自己被冤枉了。

examples.en: She argued that the contract had been unfairly drawn up.
examples.cn: 她辩称这份合同拟得不公正。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺费耳历」——俺费了耳力听完，结果还是被人占了便宜，太不公平。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ fair + 副词后缀 -ly，fair 来自古英语 fæger（美的、悦目的）

sensesIntro.en: One manner, tilted, appears in shares, accusations, contests, and court rulings.
sensesIntro.cn: 一种倾斜的方式，出现在分配、指责、比赛与判决里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the best apple handed to the same person every time.
core.cn: 核心意象：最好的苹果每次都递给同一个人。

branches.en: The shares branch: less than someone deserved.
branches.cn: 分配分支：所得少于应得。

branches.en: The accusation branch: weight pushed onto one person.
branches.cn: 指责分支：重量被压到一个人身上。

branches.en: The contest branch: rules bent for advantage.
branches.cn: 比赛分支：为占便宜而弯折规则。

branches.en: The legal branch: treatment that cannot be justified.
branches.cn: 法律分支：无法说明理由的对待。

branches.en: The manner branch: a judgement that goes too far.
branches.cn: 方式分支：过头的评判。

intro.en: Three parts, all ordinary English: prefix, adjective, adverb ending.
intro.cn: 三个部件都是常见英语：前缀、形容词、副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin layer here; fair is a native word, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这一层没有拉丁语，fair 是本土词，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 一道不公的命令被拒绝。
不平等的报酬就是不公。

definition_zh: 猛推；插入；推力；要旨
definition_en: to push something or someone suddenly and strongly, or the strong forward force that does this
core_image: 手掌平贴，一瞬间把东西直直地推出去
scene: 人群忽然向前一挤,他被推得差点撞到栏杆上。 The crowd thrust him forward against the barrier.
sceneCN: 这里 thrust 是「猛推」（第 1 个义项：突然而有力地推）；句意为人群把他猛推向前，撞上了围栏。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「推进器；推的人」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「有进取心的；向外突出的」

senses.title: To push suddenly and hard
senses.definition: to push something or someone suddenly and with force
senses.definitionCN: 突然而有力地推某物或某人
senses.example: He thrust the letter into my hand and walked off.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信硬塞到我手里就走了。
senses.why: The word comes from the Norse verb for pressing, and its first job is still the physical shove.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自北欧语中表示「压、推」的动词，最基本的用途仍是实体的猛推。

senses.title: To force something on someone
senses.definition: to make someone accept an idea, duty or position whether they want it or not
senses.definitionCN: 不管对方愿不愿意，迫使其接受想法、责任或职位
senses.example: The decision was thrust upon the small team at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定在最后一刻被硬塞给这个小团队。
senses.why: The shove becomes social: a duty is pressed onto someone who never asked for it.
senses.whyCN: 这一推变成了社会性的：一项责任被压到从没要过它的人身上。

senses.title: The force that pushes forward
senses.definition: the strong forward force made by an engine, a swimmer or an arm
senses.definitionCN: 发动机、游泳者或手臂产生的强向前之力
senses.example: The rocket’s thrust lifted it clear of the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭的推力把它推离地面。
senses.why: The noun turns the push into a measurable force, always pointing forward.
senses.whyCN: 名词把这一推变成可计量的力，方向始终向前。

senses.title: The main point of an argument
senses.definition: the main idea or aim of a plan, argument or policy
senses.definitionCN: 计划、论证或政策的主要想法或目标
senses.example: The main thrust of the report is that costs must fall.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的要旨是必须削减开支。
senses.why: An argument pushes a reader in one direction, and that direction is its thrust.
senses.whyCN: 论证把读者推向一个方向，那个方向就是它的要旨。

intro.en: Thrust came into English from Old Norse, a cousin of throw, and both share a pressing, twisting root.
intro.cn: thrust 经古北欧语进入英语，与 throw 是表亲，两者共有「压、扭」的词根。

items.en: The root carried both twisting and pressing, so the arm both turns and pushes.
items.cn: 这个词根兼含「扭」与「压」两重意味，于是手臂既转又推。

items.en: Norse þrýsta meant to press or compel, and Norse settlers brought it into English use.
items.cn: 北欧语 þrýsta 意为「压、逼迫」，由北欧移民带入英语。

items.en: Middle English used thrust for a strong push and for forcing something on someone, as in thrust into.
items.cn: 中古英语用 thrust 表示强力推动，也用于 thrust into 这类「硬塞」的表达。

items.en: The noun appeared with the machine age, naming the forward force of engines and rockets.
items.cn: 名词义随机械时代出现，用来命名发动机与火箭的向前推力。

items.en: Modern English keeps an abstract sense as well, the thrust of an argument or a policy.
items.cn: 现代英语还保留抽象义，指论证或政策的要旨。

note.en: The first group gathers the thrust family and near spellings; the second compares verbs of pushing.
note.cn: 第一组收 thrust 词族与形近词；第二组比较表示推的动词。

entries.definition: An engine or device that produces thrust.
entries.definitionCN: 推进器；产生推力的装置

entries.definition: To hurl through the air; a close relative with a long-o vowel.
Careful use of money; similar thri- opening, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 节俭；开头相似，词源不同

entries.definition: To rely on someone; one vowel apart and differently rooted.
entries.definitionCN: 信任；只差一个元音，词源不同

entries.definition: The general verb for pressing forward; plain and neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 推（最普通的说法，语气中性）

entries.definition: To push roughly, often with the hands, and informally.
To drive or push something forward, usually of engines.
To force forward or to make someone act; also the noun for motivation.
entries.definitionCN: 驱动；驱使（也作名词表示驱动力）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the Norse pressing origin and the three-way sense split.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自北欧语「压」的来源，以及三路引申的分叉。

normal.en: Thrust, thrust, thrust: the past form never changes, like cut and put.
normal.cn: thrust 的过去式与过去分词都不变化，与 cut、put 一样。

normal.en: The verb comes from a Norse word for pressing, so it is a push with weight behind it.
normal.cn: 动词源自北欧语表示「压」的词，因此这一推背后带着分量。

normal.en: A rocket’s thrust is a push you cannot see but can feel.
normal.cn: 火箭的 thrust 是看不见却能感到的推。

normal.en: The thrust of an argument is where the argument is pushing you.
normal.cn: 论证的 thrust 就是它在往哪个方向推你。

normal.en: Thrust upon means the duty was pushed onto you without asking.
normal.cn: thrust upon 意为责任被不问一声就压到你身上。

abstract.en: Picture a flat palm in one instant pushing a door all the way open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只平掌在一瞬间把门推到底。

abstract.en: One word serves the hand, the engine and the argument.
abstract.cn: 同一个词服务于手、引擎与论证。

abstract.en: Thrust is force with a direction: no pushing in circles.
abstract.cn: thrust 是有方向的力：不绕着圈推。

examples.en: She thrust the note into her pocket and ran.
examples.cn: 她把便条塞进口袋就跑。

examples.en: The engine’s thrust is measured in newtons.
examples.cn: 发动机的推力以牛顿为单位计量。

examples.en: The thrust of his speech was a call for patience.
examples.cn: 他演讲的要旨是呼吁耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死拉斯特」——死命拉着还顺手一推，力量十足 → thrust 猛推

root: 古北欧语 þrýsta「压、逼迫」进入英语，与 throw 同族，共享日耳曼词根「压、扭」；由实体猛推延伸出「强加」「（机械）推力」与「要旨」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Thrust is one strong directional push, applied by a hand, a duty, a rocket or an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: thrust 就是一次有力的定向推压，施加者可以是手、一项责任、一枚火箭或一段论证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat palm pushing a door open in one instant.
core.cn: 核心意象：平掌在一瞬间把门推到底。

branches.en: The hand: a letter shoved into a palm.
branches.cn: 手线：把信塞进掌心。

branches.en: The burden: a duty pushed onto someone.
branches.cn: 负担线：责任被推到某人身上。

branches.en: The machine: newtons of forward force.
branches.cn: 机械线：以牛顿计的向前之力。

branches.en: The argument: the direction a report pushes you.
branches.cn: 论证线：报告把你推向的方向。

branches.en: Body and engine share the same straight-line force.
branches.cn: 身体与引擎共用同一股直线之力。

intro.en: Thrust takes -er for the doer or device and -ing for the adjective and noun.
intro.cn: thrust 加 -er 表示施事者或装置，加 -ing 表示形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The word came through Old Norse with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词经古北欧语而来，没有拉丁语来源，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: one who pushes or a device

definition_zh: 昏暗的；模糊的；迟钝的；使变暗
definition_en: not bright, not clearly seen, or not quick to understand
core_image: 走廊尽头那盏灯泡蒙着灰，光只照到半面墙
scene: 走廊尽头那盏灯泡蒙着灰，人影走近才看得清。 The lamp grew dim as the evening went on.
sceneCN: 这里 dim 指「昏暗的」（第 1 个义项：光线不明亮）；句意是天色渐晚，那盏灯越来越暗。

senses.title: Giving little light
senses.definition: not bright, so that shapes are hard to see
senses.definitionCN: 光不亮，连轮廓都很难看清
senses.example: They ate supper by a dim lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一盏昏暗的灯下吃晚饭。
senses.why: The light is there, but it reaches only halfway across the room.
senses.whyCN: 光还在，只是只照到屋子的一半。

senses.title: Faint in the memory
senses.definition: remembered or seen without clear edges
senses.definitionCN: 记得或看见，却带着毛边
senses.example: I have only a dim memory of that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天我只剩一点模糊的记忆。
senses.why: The picture is still there, but the light on it has faded.
senses.whyCN: 画面还在，照在上面的光却淡了。

senses.title: Slow to understand
senses.definition: not quick at seeing or understanding something
senses.definitionCN: 看事或懂事不够快
senses.example: He was dim about the joke until everyone laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 直到大家都笑了，他才明白那个玩笑。
senses.why: The lamp inside the head burns low as well.
senses.whyCN: 脑袋里的那盏灯也烧得很暗。

intro.en: Dim comes from Old English dimm, a Germanic word for darkness that has changed very little.
intro.cn: dim 来自古英语 dimm，是一个表示黑暗的日耳曼词，形状几乎没变。

items.en: A root dim- described mist and weak light.
items.cn: 词根 dim- 形容雾气与微弱的光。

items.en: Dimm meant dark or gloomy.
items.cn: dimm 指暗、阴沉的。

items.en: The word also described eyesight that had weakened.
items.cn: 这个词也开始形容衰退的视力。

items.en: The verb sense of making a light weaker appeared.
items.cn: 「把灯调暗」的动词用法出现。

items.en: Dim now covers light, memory and slow understanding.
items.cn: 如今 dim 兼指光线、记忆与迟钝的理解。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one sound, while the meaning group offers various kinds of weak light.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音，近义组则给出几种不同的弱光。

entries.definition: a small coin worth ten cents
a loud and unpleasant noise
a switch that lowers the light
weak and barely possible to see or hear
entries.definitionCN: 微弱得几乎看不见或听不见的

entries.definition: dark and unclear, as dirty water is
entries.definitionCN: 像脏水那样暗而浑浊的

entries.definition: not bright, sharp or interesting
entries.definitionCN: 不明亮、不锋利也不有趣的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one dusty bulb and end with a mind that needs the joke explained.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只蒙灰的灯泡开始，最后落到一颗要人解释笑话的脑袋。

normal.en: Dim, dimmer, dimmest: the word itself fades as it grows.
normal.cn: dim、dimmer、dimmest：这个词自己越写越淡。

normal.en: Dim the lights and the room loses its edges.
normal.cn: 把灯调暗，屋子就丢了边。

normal.en: A dim memory is a photo left too long in the sun.
normal.cn: 模糊的记忆，是晒了太久的照片。

normal.en: Dim does not mean stupid; it means slow to catch the light.
normal.cn: dim 不等于蠢，只是接光慢一点。

normal.en: Twilight is the sky dimming without a switch.
normal.cn: 黄昏是天自己在变暗，不用开关。

abstract.en: Picture a bulb with dust on the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃上积了灰的灯泡。

abstract.en: Picture a face turning away into shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸转进阴影里。

abstract.en: Picture a path that fades before the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小路在门前就淡掉了。

examples.en: The stage was dim before the music began.
examples.cn: 音乐响起前，舞台一片昏暗。

examples.en: His dim memory of the town slowly returned.
examples.cn: 他对那座小镇的模糊记忆慢慢回来了。

examples.en: Please dim the lights a little.
examples.cn: 请把灯调暗一点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dim 记成「低暗」：灯一低，光就暗，看什么都蒙着一层。

root: 来自古英语 dimm，出自日耳曼语表示雾气与弱光的词根，千百年来形状几乎未变。本义是「暗、阴沉」，后来用于形容视力与记忆的模糊，又引申为理解迟钝；作动词时表示把光调弱。

sensesIntro.en: From a weak lamp, to a memory without edges, to a mind that catches the point late.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一盏弱灯，到一段没有边界的记忆，再到一颗迟迟才接住意思的脑袋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dusty bulb whose light stops halfway across the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只蒙灰的灯泡，光到半面墙就停住。

chain: THE EYE STRAINS FOR THE OUTLINE

branches.en: The first sense is about the light in a room.
branches.cn: 第一个义项说的是屋里的光。

branches.en: The second sense moves the weak light into memory.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把弱光挪进记忆里。

branches.en: The third sense puts the weak light inside a head.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把弱光放进一颗脑袋。

branches.en: Both are pictures missing their edges.
branches.cn: 两者都是丢了边的画面。

branches.en: A fading picture and a slow mind share one word.
branches.cn: 褪色的画面与迟缓的脑子共用一个词。

intro.en: Dim grows a small family of adverbs, nouns and switched lights.
intro.cn: dim 长出一小族词，包括副词、名词与可调的灯。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the word is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词是本土的日耳曼词。

items.example: The corridor stayed dim all day.
Two figures stood dimly at the door.
items.exampleCN: 门口隐隐站着两个人影。

items.example: Turn the dimmer down a little.
That corner is the dimmest in the house.
items.exampleCN: 那个角落是屋里最暗的。

items.example: The windows were dimmed by dust.
The dimming sky warned of rain.
items.exampleCN: 天色转暗，预示着要下雨。

items.example: He called himself a dimwit for forgetting.

definition_zh: 学期
definition_en: one of the two main periods into which a school or university year is divided
core_image: 课表上第一门课的名字刚写好，墨迹还没干
scene: 新学期开始，她在课表上写下第一门课的名字。 The new semester starts next Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 semester 是「学期」（第 1 个义项）；句意：新学期下星期一开始。

senses.title: School term
senses.definition: one of the two main teaching periods in a school year
senses.definitionCN: 学年中两个主要教学时段之一
senses.example: She took four courses this semester.
senses.exampleCN: 这学期她修了四门课。
senses.why: This is the standard school sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是学校语境中的标准义。

senses.title: University half-year
senses.definition: a period of study of about half a year at a university
senses.definitionCN: 大学中约半年的学习时段
senses.example: The exchange semester begins in March.
senses.exampleCN: 交换学期从三月开始。
senses.why: The word is especially common in higher education.
senses.whyCN: 该词在高等教育语境中尤为常用。

intro.en: Semester comes from Latin semestris, of six months, from sex six and mensis month.
intro.cn: semester 源自拉丁语 semestris（六个月的），由 sex（六）与 mensis（月）构成。

items.en: Mensis meant month.
items.cn: mensis 意为月。

items.en: Semestris meant lasting six months.
items.cn: semestris 意为持续六个月的。

items.en: German universities used Semester for a half year.
items.cn: 德国大学用 Semester 指半年。

items.en: English borrowed semester from German use.
items.cn: 英语从德语的用法中借入 semester。

items.en: American schools adopted it widely.
items.cn: 美国学校广泛采用了这个词。

note.en: Semester is compared with similar-looking words and with words for study periods.
note.cn: 把 semester 与形近词以及表示学习时段的词作比较。

entries.definition: a class for discussion
relating to a semester
a period of three months
a fixed period of study
a period when teaching takes place
the yearly period of study

normalIntro.en: Semester means half a study year, about six months.
normalIntro.cn: semester 意为半个学年，约六个月。

normal.en: Semester begins with seme, a form meaning six.
normal.cn: semester 开头 seme 这一形式表示「六」。

normal.en: Most schools have a spring and a fall semester.
normal.cn: 多数学校分春季学期与秋季学期。

normal.en: A semester abroad is a term spent overseas.
normal.cn: semester abroad 是在海外度过的一个学期。

normal.en: The adjective is semestral.
normal.cn: 形容词形式是 semestral。

normal.en: Semester is common in universities, term in schools.
normal.cn: 大学常用 semester，中小学常用 term。

abstract.en: A semester is a container for a fixed amount of learning.
abstract.cn: 学期是装载一定学习量的容器。

abstract.en: Every semester ends before everything is finished.
abstract.cn: 每个学期都在事情没做完时结束。

abstract.en: Time divided into terms can be measured and used.
abstract.cn: 把时间分成学期，就可以计量和使用。

examples.en: She took four courses this semester.
examples.cn: 这学期她修了四门课。

examples.en: The exchange semester begins in March.
examples.cn: 交换学期从三月开始。

examples.en: The new semester starts next Monday.
examples.cn: 新学期下星期一开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: semester 源自拉丁语 semestris（六个月的），由 sex（六）与 mensis（月）构成，故指约半年的学期。

root: 源自拉丁语 semestris（六个月的），由 sex（六）与 mensis（月）构成，核心义「约半年的学段」。

sensesIntro.en: Semester means a school term or a university half-year of study.
sensesIntro.cn: semester 意为学期或大学半学年。

core.en: A study period of about six months.
core.cn: 约六个月的一段学习时间。

branches.en: One of two teaching terms.
branches.cn: 两个教学学期之一。

branches.en: A half-year at a university.
branches.cn: 大学里的半个学年。

branches.en: School and university uses overlap.
branches.cn: 中小学与大学的用法相互重叠。

branches.en: Spring and fall divide the year.
branches.cn: 春季与秋季把学年分开。

branches.en: Exchange programs count study in semesters.
branches.cn: 交换项目按学期计算学习时间。

intro.en: Semester connects to Latin words for month and for six.
intro.cn: semester 与表示「月」和「六」的拉丁词相连。

latinIntro.en: Latin semestris and mensis are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 semestris 与 mensis 是历史词根。

items.example: The semestral exam is in May.

items.exampleCN: 他参加了一门为期一学期的课程。

items.example: The school runs a semestered calendar.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校实行学期制校历。
这个项目按三个月一学期运行。
课程按两个月一期分组。

items.example: The semestrial report is due soon.

latinEntries.exampleCN: sex 在拉丁语中意为六。

definition_zh: 一千；数以千计的；成千上万
definition_en: the number one thousand, or a very large number of people or things taken loosely
core_image: 一千枚小圆点排成整齐的方阵，一眼数不完
scene: 老街的夜市灯火通明,摊位前人头攒动,根本数不清。 Thousands of people crowded into the old street for the night market.
sceneCN: 这里 thousand 是「数以千计的、成千上万的」（第 2 个义项：表示数量极多）；句意为成千上万的人涌进老街逛夜市。

collocations.zh: 数以千计的；成千上万的
千中之一；罕见的人或物

derivatives.zh: 由本词加序数后缀 -th 构成，义为「第一千；千分之一」
本词的复数形式，义为「数以千计；大量」
由本词加 -fold 构成，义为「千倍的；千倍地」

senses.title: The number one thousand
senses.definition: the number equal to ten times one hundred, written as 1000
senses.definitionCN: 等于一百的十倍、写作 1000 的数
senses.example: The hall can seat a thousand guests.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能坐一千位客人。
senses.why: The word is a Germanic compound whose older meaning was a great hundred or a very large counted group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是日耳曼语复合词，较早的意义是「大百」，即一个很大的计数单位。

senses.title: Very many, loosely counted
senses.definition: a very large but unspecified number, used in the plural with of
senses.definitionCN: 数量极大但不确切，复数后接 of
senses.example: Thousands of birds stop at the lake each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天都有成千上万只鸟在这片湖上停歇。
senses.why: Once the word meant a huge round count, it easily doubled as a word for too many to count.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既然表示一个很大的整数，就很容易兼表「多到数不过来」。

senses.title: One in a thousand: rare excellence
senses.definition: in the phrase one in a thousand, a person or thing that is unusually good
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 one in a thousand，指格外好的人或物
senses.example: A helper like her is one in a thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 像她这样的帮手是千中难求的。
senses.why: Thousand sets the price of rarity: pick one out of that whole crowd and it is special.
senses.whyCN: thousand 给稀有标了价：从那么一大群中挑出一个，它就是特别的。

senses.title: Used for emphasis in repetition
senses.definition: used in phrases such as a thousand times to stress how often something happens
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a thousand times 一类短语，强调某事发生的次数之多
senses.example: I have told you a thousand times to lock the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我跟你说过无数次要把门锁好。
senses.why: The number stands in for an unmeasured repetition, a spoken exaggeration rather than a real count.
senses.whyCN: 这个数字代替的是无法计量的重复，是口语夸张而非真实计数。

intro.en: Thousand is an old Germanic compound whose first part meant swelling or great and whose second part was the word for hundred.
intro.cn: thousand 是古老的日耳曼语复合词，前半表示「膨胀、巨大」，后半就是「百」这个词。

items.en: The compound combined a root for swelling or being great with the word hundred, giving a great hundred, the biggest old unit.
items.cn: 这个复合词把表示「膨胀、巨大」的词根与 hundred 组合，构成「大百」，是古代最大的计数单位。

items.en: Old English ðusend kept both halves recognisable and still carried the sense of a vast round number.
items.cn: 古英语 ðusend 仍能辨认出两半，并保留「庞大的整数」的含义。

items.en: Norse settlers used a closely related form, which helped fix the modern th- sound and spelling.
items.cn: 北欧移民使用与之密切相关的形式，帮助固定了现代以 th- 开头的读音与拼写。

items.en: Middle English thousand settled as a plain numeral once the decimal system of counting spread.
items.cn: 十进制计数铺开之后，中古英语 thousand 固定为单纯的数词。

items.en: Modern English uses the plural thousands for loose bigness and keeps a thousand times as an exaggeration.
items.cn: 现代英语用复数 thousands 表示含糊的「极多」，并保留 a thousand times 这类夸张说法。

note.en: The first group lines up the counting words around thousand; the second compares words for very large numbers.
note.cn: 第一组排开 thousand 周边的计数词；第二组比较表示极大数量的词。

entries.definition: The ordinal, meaning the one in position one thousand.
The plural used for an unspecified large number.
The unit inside the old compound; a hundred on its own.
entries.definitionCN: 百；是古老的复合词后半，单独表示一百

entries.definition: A thousand times as much, formed with -fold.
One thousand thousands; a far larger round number.
entries.definitionCN: 百万；比千大得多的整数

entries.definition: A countless number, used formally or in literature.
Too many to be counted; it gives no exact figure at all.
entries.definitionCN: 数不清的（完全不给出数目）

entries.definition: A large enough amount; it stresses enough rather than number.
entries.definitionCN: 大量（强调充足而非计数）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the two halves of the compound and from the plural pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自这个复合词的两半，以及复数的用法规律。

normal.en: The second half is the word hundred: thousand began as a great hundred.
normal.cn: 后半就是 hundred 这个词：thousand 起初指「大百」。

normal.en: Thousands of keeps the plural -s and the preposition of.
normal.cn: thousands of 保留复数 -s 并跟介词 of。

normal.en: A thousand is exact when you count money, but loose in a thousand times.
normal.cn: 数钱时 a thousand 是精确的，在 a thousand times 里却是含糊的。

normal.en: The ordinal is thousandth, with -th, like fourth and fifth.
normal.cn: 序数词是 thousandth，加 -th，与 fourth、fifth 同类。

normal.en: One in a thousand means rare, not exactly the thousandth one.
normal.cn: one in a thousand 意为罕见，并不是恰好第一千个。

abstract.en: Picture a grid of little dots ten by ten by ten, a cube you cannot count at a glance.
abstract.cn: 想象十乘十乘十的小圆点方阵，一个一眼数不完的立方体。

abstract.en: The word is a big round stone: say it and the group it names becomes one thing.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一块圆圆的大石头：一说出口，它所命名的群体就变成一个整体。

abstract.en: Thousand is where counting stops being careful and starts being a feeling for size.
abstract.cn: thousand 是计数从认真转向「规模感」的地方。

examples.en: The old stadium holds about twenty thousand people.
examples.cn: 这座老体育场能容纳约两万人。

examples.en: Thousands of letters arrived after the programme was shown.
examples.cn: 节目播出后，成千上万封信寄来了。

examples.en: A friend like that is one in a thousand.
examples.cn: 那样的朋友是千中难求的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扫灶的」——一千个人排队扫灶，队伍长得望不到头 → thousand 一千

root: 日耳曼语复合词：前半词根表示「膨胀、巨大」，后半即 hundred「百」，合起来是古代最大的计数单位「大百」；古英语作 ðusend，古北欧语近缘形式固定了 th- 音，后随十进制普及成为单纯数词「一千」。

sensesIntro.en: Thousand moves from an exact round count to a loose bigness, then to a measure of rarity and of endless repetition.
sensesIntro.cn: thousand 从一个精确的大整数，扩展为含糊的「极多」，再引申出「稀有」与「无尽重复」两种用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cube of little dots, ten by ten by ten, too many to count in one glance.
core.cn: 核心意象：十乘十乘十的小圆点立方体，一眼数不完。

branches.en: The exact count: ten hundreds, written as a number.
branches.cn: 精确计数线：十个一百，写作一个数字。

branches.en: The loose crowd: thousands of, too many to bother counting.
branches.cn: 含糊人群线：thousands of，多到懒得去数。

branches.en: The rare one: chosen out of the whole crowd.
branches.cn: 稀有线：从整群中挑出的那一个。

branches.en: The exaggeration: a number standing in for endless repetition.
branches.cn: 夸张线：用一个数字代替无尽的重复。

branches.en: Precision and vagueness both live in the same round word.
branches.cn: 精确与含糊都住在同一个圆整的词里。

intro.en: Thousand takes the ordinal -th and the multiplier -fold; the plural -s does the rest.
intro.cn: thousand 可加序数后缀 -th 与倍数后缀 -fold，其余由复数 -s 承担。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼语来源，没有拉丁语成分，拉丁词条留空。

items.structure: second half of the old compound

definition_zh: 溶解；解散；消散
definition_en: to mix into a liquid until the solid disappears, or to end a group or marriage officially
core_image: 一块方糖落进热水，棱角一圈圈化掉，最后连影子都不剩
scene: 杯底的糖已经看不见了，只剩一圈浅浅的漩涡。 Stir the tea until the sugar dissolves.
sceneCN: 这里 dissolve 指「溶解」（第 1 个义项：固体化进液体里）；句意是搅动茶水，直到糖化开。

senses.title: To melt into a liquid
senses.definition: to mix with a liquid until the solid can no longer be seen
senses.definitionCN: 与液体混合，直到看不见固体
senses.example: Salt dissolves faster in warm water.
senses.exampleCN: 盐在温水里化得更快。
senses.why: The solid does not vanish; it simply stops having an edge.
senses.whyCN: 固体没有消失，只是失去了棱角。

senses.title: To bring a body to an end
senses.definition: to officially end a group, a parliament, or a marriage
senses.definitionCN: 正式结束一个团体、议会或婚姻
senses.example: The king dissolved parliament that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 国王在那年冬天解散了议会。
senses.why: An assembly is held together by rules, and rules can be withdrawn.
senses.whyCN: 议会靠规则聚在一起，规则一撤，人也就散了。

senses.title: To fade away
senses.definition: to disappear gradually, as if melted into the surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 像化进周围一样渐渐消失
senses.example: The crowd dissolved into the night.
senses.exampleCN: 人群散进夜色里。
senses.why: What melts leaves no pieces to count.
senses.whyCN: 化掉的东西，连碎片都数不出来。

intro.en: Dissolve comes from Latin dis-, apart, plus solvere, to loosen: a knot undone until nothing holds.
intro.cn: dissolve 来自拉丁语 dis-（分开）加 solvere（松开），画面是一个结被彻底解开。

items.en: Solvere meant to loosen, untie or set free.
items.cn: solvere 指松开、解开或释放。

items.en: Dis- added the sense of apart, so the loosening went all the way through.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 加上分开之意，松开就变得彻底。

items.en: Dissolvere described a solid losing its shape in liquid.
items.cn: dissolvere 描绘固体在液体里失去形状。

items.en: English borrowed it for melting and for ending an assembly.
items.cn: 英语借入后既指化开，也指解散集会。

items.en: Writers stretched it to crowds and feelings fading away.
items.cn: 文人把它扩展到人群与情绪渐渐消散。

items.en: Today a tablet, a parliament and a marriage can all dissolve.
items.cn: 今天药片、议会与婚姻都可以用这个词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the solve stem, while the meaning group gathers other ways of coming apart.
note.cn: 形近组共享 solve 这段词干，近义组则是几个表示化开或散去的词。

entries.definition: to find an answer to a problem
an answer, or a liquid with something mixed in
entries.definitionCN: 答案，或溶有他物的液体

entries.definition: a liquid that can dissolve other things
to turn from solid to liquid through heat
to break up a group or band
to grow faint and slowly disappear

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep one picture in view: a lump that loses its edges until nothing is left to hold.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守住一幅画面：一块东西失去棱角，最后什么也抓不住。

normal.en: Dis- plus solve: the knot is fully loosened.
normal.cn: dis 加 solve，就是把这个结彻底松开。

normal.en: Sugar in hot tea shows the whole process in a minute.
normal.cn: 热茶里的糖一分钟就演完全过程。

normal.en: A tablet dissolves and the water stays clear.
normal.cn: 药片化开，水还是清的。

normal.en: Parliament dissolves, and the benches empty by evening.
normal.cn: 议会一解散，傍晚椅子就空了。

normal.en: The crowd dissolved, and the square went quiet.
normal.cn: 人群散去，广场安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a cube of ice losing its corners.
abstract.cn: 想象一块冰先失去四个角。

abstract.en: Picture a knot pulled until the rope is straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结被拉到绳子笔直。

abstract.en: Picture chalk marks washed off a blackboard.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上的粉笔字被水冲掉。

examples.en: Sugar dissolves quickly in hot water.
examples.cn: 糖在热水里化得很快。

examples.en: The new law dissolved the old committee.
examples.cn: 新法律解散了旧委员会。

examples.en: The crowd dissolved into the dark streets.
examples.cn: 人群散进黑暗的街道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dissolve 记成「松开就化」：dis 表示分开，solve 表示松开，一松开，固体就化进水里，团体也就散了。

root: 源自拉丁语 dissolvere，由表示分开的 dis- 与表示松开的 solvere 组成，本义是把结解开、把整体拆散。英语先用来指固体化进液体，也指正式解散机构或婚姻，后来引申为渐渐消散。

sensesIntro.en: From a solid losing its edges in water to a group losing its rules and drifting apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 从固体在水里失去棱角，到一个团体失去规则、各自走散。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sugar cube sinking in hot tea, its edges softening until nothing is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块方糖沉进热茶，棱角慢慢软掉，最后什么都不剩。

branches.en: The first sense is the solid vanishing into the liquid.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是固体化进液体里不见了。

branches.en: The second sense ends an official body by removing its rules.
branches.cn: 第二个义项靠撤掉规则来结束一个正式机构。

branches.en: The third sense lets a crowd thin out until the place is empty.
branches.cn: 第三个义项让人群渐渐稀疏，直到场地空了。

branches.en: Both senses undo something that was held together.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在拆开原本聚在一起的东西。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs a formal decision by an authority.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要权威方面作出正式决定。

intro.en: Dissolve belongs to the solve family, where Latin solvere, to loosen, meets several prefixes.
intro.cn: dissolve 属于 solve 一族，中心是拉丁语 solvere（松开），前后接上不同前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere, to loosen, gives solve, solution and solvent; dis- pulls the loosening apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solvere（松开）给出 solve、solution 与 solvent，前缀 dis- 把松开推向彻底分开。

items.meaning: to loosen apart until the solid is gone
to loosen a problem and find the answer
the answer, or a liquid mixture
a liquid that loosens other substances
the act of dissolving or ending
items.example: The dissolution of the firm took a year.
Undissolved salt lay at the bottom.

definition_zh: 重力；地心引力；严重性
definition_en: the force that pulls things to the earth, or seriousness
core_image: 苹果从枝头垂直落下
scene: 苹果受重力作用落向地面。 An apple falls to the ground because of gravity.
sceneCN: 这里 gravity 是「重力、地心引力」（第 1 个义项）；句意：苹果受重力作用落向地面。

senses.title: The force of falling
senses.definition: the force that pulls objects towards the earth
senses.definitionCN: 把物体拉向地球的力
senses.example: An apple falls to the ground because of gravity.
senses.exampleCN: 苹果受重力作用落向地面。
senses.why: The physical force is the dominant modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 物理之力是现代最主要的义项。

senses.title: Seriousness
senses.definition: the seriousness of a situation
senses.definitionCN: 局势的严重程度
senses.example: He did not grasp the gravity of the situation.
senses.exampleCN: 他没有意识到局势的严重性。
senses.why: A heavy situation is felt as grave.
senses.whyCN: 沉重的事态被感受为严重。

senses.title: Dignified manner
senses.definition: a quiet and dignified manner
senses.definitionCN: 安静而庄重的举止
senses.example: She spoke with quiet gravity.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着平静的庄重说话。
senses.why: Weight becomes dignity in a person.
senses.whyCN: 重量在人的身上变成庄重。

intro.en: Gravity comes from Latin gravitas, weight and dignity.
intro.cn: gravity 来自拉丁语 gravitas，意为重量与庄重。

items.en: Gravis meant heavy.
items.cn: gravis 意为沉重的。

items.en: Gravitas meant weight and dignity.
items.cn: gravitas 意为重量与庄重。

items.en: Gravité carried the sense of seriousness.
items.cn: gravité 带有严肃之义。

items.en: Gravity named the force of falling.
items.cn: gravity 指使物体下落的力。

items.en: Newton's work fixed the physical sense.
items.cn: 牛顿的工作确立了它的物理义。

note.en: Gravity is compared with look-alike words and words for weight.
note.cn: 把 gravity 与形近词以及表示重量的词作比较。

entries.definition: seriously
the feeling of thanks
a burial place
how heavy something is
the state of being serious
a force drawing something

normalIntro.en: Gravity is the earth's long arm pulling everything down.
normalIntro.cn: gravity 就是地球伸出的长手，把一切都往下拉。

normal.en: Gravity pulls the ball down.
normal.cn: 重力把球往下拉。

normal.en: Astronauts float in zero gravity.
normal.cn: 宇航员在失重中漂浮。

normal.en: He understood the gravity of the news.
normal.cn: 他明白这消息有多严重。

normal.en: The centre of gravity is low.
normal.cn: 重心很低。

normal.en: She spoke with gravity.
normal.cn: 她说话很庄重。

abstract.en: Gravity is the quiet promise that things come down.
abstract.cn: 重力，是万物终将落下的安静承诺。

abstract.en: Some words have their own gravity.
abstract.cn: 有些话自带重力。

abstract.en: The heavier the truth, the softer the voice.
abstract.cn: 真相越重，声音越轻。

examples.en: An apple falls to the ground because of gravity.
examples.cn: 苹果受重力作用落向地面。

examples.en: He did not grasp the gravity of the situation.
examples.cn: 他没有意识到局势的严重性。

examples.en: She spoke with quiet gravity.
examples.cn: 她带着平静的庄重说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: gravity 与 grave（严重的）、gravely（严重地）同根，词根意为「沉重」；force of gravity 是重力，zero gravity 是失重，centre of gravity 是重心。

root: 来自拉丁语 gravitas（重量、庄重），词根 gravis 意为沉重，核心义由物理的重量扩展到事态的严重性与人的庄重。

sensesIntro.en: Gravity means the force of falling, the seriousness of a situation, or dignified manner.
sensesIntro.cn: gravity 指重力、局势的严重性，或庄重的举止。

core.en: Weight that pulls, whether of matter or meaning.
core.cn: 向下拉的重，无论是物还是意义。

branches.en: An apple drops straight down.
branches.cn: 苹果笔直落下。

branches.en: A report lies heavy on the table.
branches.cn: 一份报告沉甸甸地压在桌上。

branches.en: A person stands still and calm.
branches.cn: 一个人静立而沉稳。

branches.en: Physical weight becomes the weight of news.
branches.cn: 物理的重量，变成消息的重量。

branches.en: Serious matters make serious faces.
branches.cn: 严重的事，让人严肃。

intro.en: Gravity forms adjectives, verbs, and compounds.
intro.cn: gravity 构成形容词、动词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is gravitas, weight.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 gravitas，意为重量。

items.example: People gravitate to the warm fire.
items.exampleCN: 人们被温暖的火吸引过去。
故事里想象了反重力靴。

definition_zh: 连续不断地；不停地；接连地
definition_en: in a way that goes on without any pause or gap
core_image: 水龙头一直滴着水，杯子慢慢被填满
scene: 实验记录上，温度曲线没有一处断点。 The sensor recorded the temperature continuously for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 continuously 指「不间断地」（第 1 个义项：在时间上没有中断）；句意是传感器连续一周不间断地记录温度。

pos.zh: 连续不断地；不停地；接连地

senses.title: Without pause
senses.definition: with no break in time at all
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上完全没有中断
senses.example: The pump runs continuously.
senses.exampleCN: 泵不停地运转。
senses.why: A watch that never stops is the simplest proof of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一只从不停走的表，就是这个义项最简单的证明。

senses.title: At every moment
senses.definition: at each moment, without any exception
senses.definitionCN: 每一刻都如此，没有任何例外
senses.example: She was continuously aware of the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 她始终留意着那只钟。
senses.why: Attention that never blinks is rare and heavy.
senses.whyCN: 从不眨眼的注意力既罕见又沉重。

senses.title: In an unbroken series
senses.definition: one after another with no empty space between
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个，之间没有空档
senses.example: Applications arrived continuously all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 整个上午申请接连不断地送来。
senses.why: A queue with no empty spot looks like one long body.
senses.whyCN: 没有空位的队伍，看起来像一个长长的身体。

intro.en: Continuously is the adverb built from continuous, which comes from Latin continuus, unbroken, and before that from continere, to hold together.
intro.cn: continuously 是由 continuous 加副词词尾构成的副词，continuous 来自拉丁语 continuus（不断开的），更早出自 continere（保持在一起）。

items.en: Continere meant to hold parts together without a gap.
items.cn: continere 意为把各部分无空隙地保持在一起。

items.en: Continuus described anything that runs on unbroken.
items.cn: continuus 形容任何不断延续的事物。

items.en: The adverb ending -e marked how an action was done.
items.cn: 拉丁语的副词词尾 -e 表示动作进行的方式。

items.en: English continuous gained the adverb form continuously.
items.cn: 英语 continuous 衍生出副词形式 continuously。

items.en: The adverb was used for motion, time and supply.
items.cn: 这个副词被用于运动、时间与供应。

items.en: It now often appears in technical and scientific writing.
items.cn: 如今它常出现在技术与科学写作中。

note.en: The look-alike group places the adverb beside its adjective and verb, and the meaning group names other adverbs of unbroken action.
note.cn: 形近组把这个副词与它的形容词、动词放在一起，近义组列出其他表示不间断的副词。

entries.definition: going on with no break
happening again and again
kept going over a period
all the time, again and again
in a regular way that does not change
without stopping at all

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow a clock that never stops, then an attention that never blinks and a queue with no empty spot.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子跟着一只不停的钟，再到从不眨眼的留意，最后到没有空位的队伍。

normal.en: Continuous plus -ly makes the manner word: in an unbroken way.
normal.cn: continuous 加 -ly 就成了方式副词：以不断开的方式。

normal.en: If the tap never closes, it drips continuously.
normal.cn: 水龙头一直不关，就连续不断地滴。

normal.en: The adverb answers how, not how long.
normal.cn: 这个副词回答的是怎样，不是多久。

normal.en: A machine that runs day and night runs continuously.
normal.cn: 日夜运转的机器就是不停地运转。

normal.en: No gap, no pause, no empty place.
normal.cn: 没有缺口，没有停顿，没有空位。

abstract.en: Picture a second hand sweeping with no pause.
abstract.cn: 想象秒针一刻不停地扫过表盘。

abstract.en: Picture a row of beads touching edge to edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一串珠子边碰着边。

abstract.en: Picture a printer laying one unbroken band of ink.
abstract.cn: 想象打印机铺出一条不断的墨带。

examples.en: The engine has run continuously since morning.
examples.cn: 这台发动机从早上起就一直运转。

examples.en: The staff monitored the screen continuously.
examples.cn: 工作人员持续盯着屏幕。

examples.en: Rain fell continuously for two days.
examples.cn: 雨连续不断地下了两天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 continuously 记成 continuous（连续的）加 ly（副词尾）：以没有断口的方式做下去，就是连续不断地。

root: 由 continuous（连续的）加副词词尾 -ly 构成，continuous 源出拉丁语 continuus（不断开的）与 continere（保持在一起）。

sensesIntro.en: From a clock that never stops, to attention at every moment, and at last to a series with no empty space.
sensesIntro.cn: 从永不停走的钟，到每一刻都在的留意，最后到没有空档的一连串。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second hand sweeping the dial with no pause.
core.cn: 核心意象：秒针毫无停顿地扫过表盘。

branches.en: The basic sense simply removes every pause.
branches.cn: 基本义项只是把每一处停顿都去掉。

branches.en: The second sense keeps watch at every moment.
branches.cn: 第二个义项在每一刻都保持留意。

branches.en: The third sense lines events up without a gap.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把事件排成没有空档的一列。

branches.en: No pause and no exception point the same way.
branches.cn: 没有停顿与没有例外指向同一个方向。

branches.en: Steady watching turns a set of events into one stream.
branches.cn: 稳定的注视把一串事件看成一条流。

intro.en: Continuously is continuous plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: continuously 由 continuous 加副词词尾 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The holding base tin- runs through continuous, continual and continuity.
latinIntro.cn: 握持词基 tin- 贯穿 continuous、continual 与 continuity。

items.exampleCN: 一再的延误让他们恼火。

items.example: The show continued after the break.
The discontinuance of the service was sudden.
items.exampleCN: 这项服务的停止很突然。

definition_zh: 静电；静态的；静电干扰
definition_en: electricity that gathers on a surface, staying still rather than flowing as a current, or noise caused by it
core_image: 毛衣上噼啪作响的小火花
scene: 干燥的空气容易产生静电。 Dry air easily produces static.
sceneCN: 这里 static 是「静电」（第 1 个义项）；句意：干燥的空气容易产生静电。

senses.title: Charge at rest
senses.definition: electric charge that gathers on a surface and does not flow
senses.definitionCN: 聚集在表面、不流动的电荷
senses.example: Dry air easily produces static.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的空气容易产生静电。
senses.why: The concrete electrical sense is the base.
senses.whyCN: 具体的电学含义，是这个字的基础。

senses.title: Not moving
